title: Synthetic Diamonds
subtitle: It is best to offer suggestions rather than commands. Always ensure that the other person is allowed to speak for themselves.

items.text: Synthetic Diamonds
Inside the Car

items.speaker: Fleming
items.text: I should've trusted you sooner, Brette. You really saved my bacon back there.

items.speaker: Fleming
items.text: I never imagined things could go this smoothly. That client you introduced me to was perfect; my first shipment is already out.

items.speaker: Tennant
items.text: I believe my fee was ten percent of the deal, cash.
Fleming leans closer, locking eyes with Tennant.

items.speaker: Fleming
items.text: I was waiting to see when you'd name your price.
Fleming bursts into a belly laugh, then pulls a thick stack of bills from his coat and hands it over.

items.speaker: Fleming
items.text: There's no better conversation than one that ends with money—and no easier conversation partner than someone who wants yours.

items.speaker: Fleming
items.text: Say, you'd call yourself a businessperson, wouldn't you?

items.speaker: Tennant
items.text: Last time I checked.

items.speaker: Fleming
items.text: Ah, but I get the feeling you've got something else going. What's your real angle?

items.speaker: Tennant
items.text: Research. Pointless research, I'm afraid. Far from profitable.

items.speaker: Fleming
items.text: Research?

items.speaker: Tennant
items.text: It isn't worth wasting words.
The car comes to a steady stop at the curb.

items.speaker: Tennant
items.text: I should go. Best of luck with your business, Fleming.

items.speaker: Fleming
items.text: You live here? Do you mind if I were to swing by sometime?

items.speaker: Tennant
items.text: I'm out, Mr. Fleming.

items.speaker: Fleming
items.text: Huh?

items.speaker: Tennant
items.text: I have no intention of digging myself deeper into the arms trade. This was just a means to an end.

items.speaker: Fleming
items.text: No, wait.

items.speaker: Fleming
items.text: Can't I just come by as a new friend?

items.speaker: Tennant
items.text: Allow me to stress this: I'm not interested.

items.speaker: Fleming
items.text: Not about business. Just a drink. Conversation.

items.speaker: Fleming
items.text: Maybe we'll find other ways to work together.

items.speaker: Tennant
items.text: If you insist, we can go upstairs and talk.
Synthetic Diamond Lab
The room is nothing like what Fleming imagined.
No heavy grandfather clock in the corner, no mounted trophies on the walls, no spacious, luxurious sofa in sight.

items.speaker: Tennant
items.text: I'm afraid I'm far from set up to entertain guests. This is a lab, not a parlor.

items.speaker: Fleming
items.text: You actually live here?
Tennant sighs helplessly and sets the cash she just received on the table.

items.speaker: Tennant
items.text: Every franc I earn goes into the instruments and materials in this room.

items.speaker: Tennant
items.text: Seven hundred and fifty thousand francs, so far.
Fleming's face twitches, his scars contorting with it.

items.speaker: Fleming
items.text: What could possibly be worth that much?

items.speaker: Tennant
items.text: We really shouldn't talk business, Fleming. Besides, I worry you'll start comparing me to Adelita.

items.speaker: Fleming
items.text: What does that fraud have to do with this? C'mon, Brette, let me in on this thing.

items.speaker: Fleming
items.text: You're a smart gal. If you've spent three-quarters of a million francs on this place. Well, I refuse to believe it's something foolish.
Reluctantly, Tennant picks up a clear beaker and swirls it, the crisp clink echoing through the lab.
Tiny sparks glimmer at the bottom.

items.speaker: Tennant
items.text: These are diamonds. But they weren't mined from any pit.

items.speaker: Tennant
items.text: The raw material is nothing more than charcoal. And they were made right here, in this little room.

items.speaker: Fleming
items.text: ... Give me a break, diamonds, really?!
Tennant sets the beaker back down and covers it with a handkerchief.

items.speaker: Tennant
items.text: See, Fleming? This is why I didn't want to talk about it.

items.speaker: Tennant
items.text: I assume you think this is just another scam.

items.speaker: Fleming
items.text: No ... no, not at all!

items.speaker: Fleming
items.text: Now I see. This is why you exposed Adelita's trick so quickly.

items.speaker: Fleming
items.text: You're exactly who you say you are. An expert in your trade.

items.speaker: Fleming
items.text: You and that fraudster are nothing alike. I can feel it.

items.speaker: Fleming
items.text: You're calm, disciplined. My friend, you're a—yes, a scientist. A true scientist.

items.speaker: Fleming
items.text: And this is one hell of a science. Diamonds from charcoal. I've heard of the idea before.

items.speaker: Fleming
items.text: Tell me, Brette. Who else knows this technique?

items.speaker: Tennant
items.text: For now, just you and me.

items.speaker: Fleming
items.text: And once they're made ... they stay diamonds?

items.speaker: Tennant
items.text: ... I've never seen one turn back into charcoal.
Fleming steps forward, lifts the handkerchief without asking, and peers into the beaker.
The diamonds refract the light, dazzling in his eyes.
He breathes hard, squinting.

items.speaker: Fleming
items.text: We could do something big with this, Brette. Growing diamonds! Just think of the money!

items.speaker: Tennant
items.text: We would need more than this lab. To produce anything at capacity and make it cost-effective, we'd need a proper factory.

items.speaker: Fleming
items.text: Then tell me—how much to turn your little lab into an underground factory?

items.speaker: Tennant
items.text: Tennant takes a long moment to form her answer.

items.speaker: Tennant
items.text: Ten million francs.
